title: MIGRA-IA: Intelligent agent for obsolescence diagnosis and migration of industrial automation systems
description: The agent can be tried online, with nothing to install and no API key, at https://migra-ia.onrender.com — it is the interactive demo of the artifact itself; if the service is asleep, the first load may take about a minute. MIGRA-IA is an assisted conversational agent that guides technical staff step by step through the diagnosis of hardware obsolescence (PLCs, I/O modules, HMIs, industrial networks, drives) and through migration planning. It implements an adaptive questionnaire, a weighted obsolescence risk scoring engine (0–100), a traceable case file with an audit trail, mandatory safety rules and human validation. It includes a reproducible demonstration mode that runs without an API key (an independently evaluable artifact). Version 0.3.0 added the structured knowledge base MIGRA-IA-GUIA-001 (6 methodological stages, 24 chapters, migration routes for 5 manufacturers, 20 verification tests, 22 templates and 5 case studies), which the agent queries through a dedicated tool. Version 0.4.0 adds a platform catalog of 30 manufacturers and 469 models, the migration procedure MIGRA-IA-PROC-050 (50 numbered steps plus 7 preliminary ones, in 7 phases), the diagnostic questionnaire extended to 17 sections and an interactive mode that runs with no API key; it withdraws the guided demonstration mode, leaving the interface with two entry points, and incorporates a reproducible ordinal risk baseline with its frozen split. It also adds two routes that specialize the procedure according to the case: the manufacturer route when staying with the same brand, and the cross-manufacturer porting route when the target is from another brand and the source program is accessible and verified, which covers the internal memory inventory and the language census, the instruction equivalence table between both manufacturers, the triage of logic that can be carried over versus logic that must be rewritten, the address mapping from the original symbol table and the behavior comparison against the starting program, with the explicit limit that the agent does not publish equivalences it cannot cite. Version 0.5.0 publishes the artifact in two languages — code, data, documentation, installation guides, interface and demonstration in Spanish and English, each document entirely in one language — and fixes a defect that interrupted the demonstration when the equipment's life-cycle status was declared unknown.
